title: Bronchiectasis (adult, non-cystic fibrosis)
subject: respiratory
summary: Confirm on thin-section CT, test for causes (immunoglobulins, ABPA, NTM), teach airway clearance to all, treat exacerbations with 14 days of culture-guided antibiotics, offer eradication for new Pseudomonas, and give long-term macrolide or inhaled antibiotic to patients at high risk of exacerbations (ERS 2025, BTS 2019).

sections.title: Recognise
items: Suspect with a persistent or recurrent productive cough for more than 8 weeks, recurrent chest infections or haemoptysis; also in COPD with frequent exacerbations and Pseudomonas, severe asthma, rheumatoid arthritis or IBD with chronic productive cough.
Diagnosis: bronchial dilatation on thin-section chest CT (broncho-arterial ratio above 1, lack of tapering, airways visible near the pleura) with compatible symptoms.
Exacerbation: worsening beyond day-to-day variation that needs a change in treatment: more cough, sputum volume or purulence, breathlessness, fatigue or haemoptysis.

Severe exacerbation (needs admission or IV antibiotics): tachypnoea, respiratory failure, falling saturation, hypercapnia, significant haemoptysis, cyanosis, new cor pulmonale, haemodynamic instability or confusion.
High risk of future exacerbations (ERS 2025): 2 or more exacerbations in the past year, or 1 severe exacerbation, or 1 exacerbation plus a high daily symptom burden.

sections.title: Investigations at diagnosis
items: All patients: FBC with blood eosinophils; serum IgG, IgA and IgM; total IgE with Aspergillus-specific IgE and IgG (ABPA); sputum for routine bacterial culture and mycobacterial smear and culture.
High NTM risk (nodules, cavities, tree-in-bud change, weight loss): at least 3 sputum samples or a bronchoalveolar lavage for mycobacteria.

Targeted tests: alpha-1 antitrypsin (basal emphysema, severe obstruction); CF (sweat test, CFTR genetics) and primary ciliary dyskinesia testing when features suggest; rheumatoid and connective tissue serology; HIV where relevant.
Spirometry, severity scoring (Bronchiectasis Severity Index or FACED), and pneumococcal antibody levels if antibody deficiency is suspected.

sections.title: Stable disease
items: Teach airway clearance to every patient (active cycle of breathing, oscillating PEP devices, postural drainage) via a respiratory physiotherapist; personalise technique and increase frequency during exacerbations.
Pulmonary rehabilitation for breathlessness or reduced exercise capacity; encourage regular physical activity.

Mucoactive treatment if airway clearance alone does not control symptoms: nebulised hypertonic saline (first dose under supervision with an airway challenge; bronchodilator pre-treatment if reactive) or oral carbocisteine (6-month trial). Do not use rhDNase.

High exacerbation risk despite standard care (any organism, including Pseudomonas): long-term macrolide, typically azithromycin 250 mg three times weekly, 250 mg daily or 500 mg three times weekly. Exclude NTM first.

Chronic Pseudomonas with high exacerbation risk: long-term inhaled antibiotic (colistimethate first line; gentamicin or tobramycin as alternatives) after a supervised test dose. A macrolide is an alternative if inhaled therapy is not tolerated.
No routine inhaled corticosteroid unless there is coexisting asthma or COPD. Offer a long-acting bronchodilator trial for significant breathlessness.
Influenza and pneumococcal vaccination; a written self-management plan, and a standby antibiotic course for selected patients.

sections.title: Exacerbations
items: Send sputum for culture before antibiotics; choose therapy from previous sputum results, local resistance patterns and severity. Repeat culture if there is no response.

A 14-day course is standard, and always for Pseudomonas or severe exacerbations. Shorter courses may suffice for mild disease, sensitive organisms (for example S. pneumoniae) or rapid return to baseline.
No previous bacteriology: amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily, or clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily if penicillin allergic, for 14 days.

Known Pseudomonas: ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily orally (750 mg twice daily if more severe). IV: ceftazidime 2 g, piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g or meropenem 2 g, each three times daily, with or without an aminoglycoside.

Other organisms by sensitivity: beta-lactamase positive H. influenzae or Moraxella: co-amoxiclav 625 mg three times daily; MSSA: flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily; MRSA: doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, or IV vancomycin or teicoplanin.
Haemoptysis of 10 mL or less in 24 hours: treat as an exacerbation with an oral antibiotic. Larger or ongoing bleeding needs emergency admission (see the massive haemoptysis protocol).

sections.title: Pseudomonas eradication
items: Offer eradication for a new isolation of P. aeruginosa (first isolate, or regrowth after a prolonged negative period).

BTS first line: ciprofloxacin 500 to 750 mg twice daily for 2 weeks. Second line: IV anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam with or without an IV aminoglycoside for 2 weeks. Either may be followed by 3 months of nebulised colistimethate, gentamicin or tobramycin.
Recheck sputum cultures afterwards; if infection becomes chronic and exacerbations are frequent, move to long-term inhaled antibiotic therapy.

sections.title: Monitoring on long-term therapy
items: Before a long-term macrolide: at least one negative NTM culture, ECG for QTc, liver tests, review of other QT-prolonging drugs, and caution with hearing loss or balance problems.
Prescribe long-term inhaled or oral antibiotics for a defined period and formally review exacerbation frequency, symptoms and side effects; stop if ineffective or poorly tolerated.
Stable patients: regular sputum culture (including periodic mycobacterial culture on macrolides) and spirometry. Monitor renal function and hearing with inhaled aminoglycosides.

sections.title: Refer to a specialist
items: Chronic Pseudomonas, NTM or MRSA infection; 3 or more exacerbations a year; long-term antibiotic therapy; declining lung function.
Associated rheumatoid arthritis, immunodeficiency, IBD, primary ciliary dyskinesia or ABPA.

Transplant discussion: FEV1 below 30% with significant instability or rapid deterioration; earlier with massive haemoptysis, severe pulmonary hypertension, ICU admissions or respiratory failure needing NIV.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Antibody deficiency (low IgG or poor pneumococcal vaccine response): refer to immunology; immunoglobulin replacement may be needed.
ABPA: treat per ABPA guidance (oral corticosteroid, with antifungal in selected patients) and monitor total IgE.
NTM pulmonary disease: specialist multidrug treatment; never give macrolide monotherapy.

India: post-tuberculous bronchiectasis is common and NTEP treats cough of 2 weeks or more as presumptive TB, so exclude active TB (sputum smear and NAAT such as Xpert MTB/RIF) before blaming bronchiectasis and avoid empirical fluoroquinolone monotherapy.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Starting long-term azithromycin without excluding NTM (risk of macrolide-resistant NTM).
Short 5-day courses for Pseudomonas exacerbations.
Routine inhaled corticosteroids without asthma or COPD.
Never teaching airway clearance, the cornerstone of treatment.
Missing immunodeficiency, ABPA or CF in younger adults.

drugs.name: Azithromycin (long-term)
drugs.dose: 250 mg orally three times weekly (alternatives: 250 mg daily or 500 mg three times weekly)
drugs.notes: High exacerbation risk. Exclude NTM, check QTc and liver tests; caution with hearing loss.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally three times daily for 14 days
drugs.notes: Empirical first line for exacerbations with no previous bacteriology.

drugs.name: Clarithromycin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally twice daily for 14 days
drugs.notes: Penicillin allergy. Many interactions; QT prolongation.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally twice daily for 14 days (750 mg twice daily if more severe)
drugs.notes: Pseudomonas exacerbation or 2-week eradication. Reduce dose in renal impairment; tendon and QT risks.

drugs.name: Ceftazidime
drugs.dose: 2 g IV three times daily for 14 days
drugs.notes: IV Pseudomonas treatment; adjust for renal function.

drugs.name: Piperacillin-tazobactam
drugs.dose: 4.5 g IV three times daily for 14 days
drugs.notes: IV Pseudomonas treatment; adjust for renal function.

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.dose: 100 mg orally twice daily for 14 days
drugs.notes: Alternative for S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae and oral MRSA option.

drugs.name: Carbocisteine
drugs.dose: 750 mg orally three times daily, reducing to 750 mg twice daily on response
drugs.notes: Trial for 6 months; continue only if there is clear benefit.
